self.disposition: 7-item Self-Review checklist completed and recorded in the iterate ADR's Self-Review section (Spec Compliance, Error Handling, Security Basics, Test Quality, Performance Basics, Naming & Structure, Affected Boundaries).

findings.finding: The plan has no data-migration story for in-flight runs. Any run created before this change whose state JSON contains `current_step`/`completed_steps` but empty or partial `phase_tasks[]` will, after this ships, have a v1 `update_step` call retargeted to a list that doesn't reflect its actual progress. Retargeting "first" makes this worse, not better — the retargeted writer will overwrite/stamp `phase_tasks[]` based on its own bookkeeping while the run's historical progress lives only in the dropped fields.
findings.suggestion: Either (a) define a one-time normalization on read/load that reconstructs `phase_tasks[]` from `current_step`/`completed_steps` for pre-existing runs, or (b) explicitly state that only runs started post-s4 are in scope and old runs are terminal/abandoned. Silence here is the biggest break-risk in the change.

findings.finding: "Retarget first, then delete" is described as sequential but scoped as a single diff. If both happen in one PR, the retarget is unobservable — there's no window where the retargeted path runs in production before the fields are dropped, so a bug in the retarget is discovered only after the old fields (the recovery source) are gone. The ordering rationale only pays off if the retarget ships separately.
findings.suggestion: Either split into two diffs (retarget + grep-gate, then drop), or keep one diff but add a test asserting the v1 path produces a `phase_tasks[]` state equivalent to what the v2 path would have produced for the same inputs, before the deletion lands.

findings.finding: The acceptance criteria say "no reader anywhere keys on current_step or completed_steps" but the plan only mentions grep as evidence. Grep misses dynamic key access (`state[fieldName]`, `getattr`, JSON consumers outside the repo — dashboards, exports, webhooks, scripts, log-based analytics keyed on those fields). If any external consumer reads the emitted run state, dropping the fields silently breaks it.
findings.suggestion: Enumerate the consumers explicitly (internal grep + a documented list of external/schema consumers), and confirm the docs schema block is the only external contract. If there's an API or event emission that includes the run state, version-bump or note the breaking change.

findings.finding: The retargeted `update_step` must decide what "advance" means against `phase_tasks[]` — append, mark-complete-next, set index? Off-by-one or idempotency semantics (what happens on a retried/duplicate update_step call?) are unspecified. If v1 callers can retry, a non-idempotent append will corrupt the list.
findings.suggestion: Specify the retarget semantics in the plan and cover the duplicate-call case with a test, matching whatever v2 already does.

findings.finding: No mention of updating or adding tests for the v1 path itself. If existing tests assert on `current_step`/`completed_steps` output, they'll fail at deletion time — fine — but the plan should state that test updates are in-scope, otherwise the "drop is mechanical" claim is misleading.
findings.suggestion: Add "tests referencing the old fields are updated in the same diff" to the acceptance criteria.

findings.finding: The plan says to “advance `phase_tasks[]`” but does not define the mapping from v1 `update_step` inputs to a task (task identity, ordering, completion state, and terminal behavior). Retargeting without preserving v1’s exact progression semantics can silently advance the wrong task or skip one.
findings.suggestion: Specify the canonical lookup and mutation rules, including how `update_step` identifies the active task and what constitutes an already-completed or final step.

findings.finding: Removing both persisted fields can break existing in-flight runs, stored snapshots, fixtures, or externally supplied v1 payloads that still contain only `current_step`/`completed_steps`. A source grep cannot establish compatibility for data written before deployment.
findings.suggestion: Establish the deployed-data strategy before deletion: migrate persisted records, derive `phase_tasks[]` when loading legacy records for one release, or explicitly prove no persisted/in-flight state survives the rollout.

findings.finding: “No reader anywhere” needs to cover more than application code: schemas/types, validators, serializers/deserializers, fixtures, test assertions, API contracts, generated artifacts, and operational scripts may encode the old fields without acting as ordinary readers. The mini-plan does not name these surfaces.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit repository-wide inventory and update list, then run targeted tests for v1 updates and serialization/validation boundaries after removal.

findings.finding: The plan does not address repeated or out-of-order `update_step` calls. If `phase_tasks[]` is mutated by index or inferred “next incomplete” task, retries/concurrent hook events may mark multiple tasks complete or regress state.
findings.suggestion: Preserve idempotency with a stable task/step identifier and test duplicate, skipped, final-step, and concurrent/replayed update events.

findings.finding: Updating the documentation schema in the same diff is necessary, but the plan lacks a verification that the documented `phase_tasks[]` shape matches the runtime schema after old-field emission is removed. Drift here would mislead hook implementers immediately.
findings.suggestion: Derive the documentation block from the authoritative schema where feasible, or add a focused contract test/review check comparing the documented fields to emitted payloads.  Overall, retargeting before deletion is the right direction, but the plan needs an explicit legacy-state compatibility decision and precise v1-to-task progression semantics before the drop is safe. The proposed grep is useful verification, not sufficient migration evidence.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

plan.disposition: All findings recorded and dispositioned in the iterate ADR's External-Plan-Review-Findings table (legacy-state migration, idempotency, doc-consumer inventory all addressed and fixed).

findings.finding: The new phase_tasks[] seed {"phase": "project", "splitId": None, "status": "awaiting_launch"} was missing every other field PhaseTask.required mandates (phaseTaskId, sessionUuid, version, title, slashCommand, prerequisites, executionCount, createdAt). _upsert_v1_phase_task only ever mutates status/startedAt/completedAt on a match, so the incomplete shape would have persisted indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Build the seed via a small local full-shape helper mirroring build_v1_phase_task's fields.

findings.finding: Docstring still said "completed_steps is left untouched" -- a stale reference to a field this same diff retires everywhere else, inconsistent with constants.py's already-updated phrasing.
findings.suggestion: Update the docstring to match constants.py's phase_tasks[]-primary/completed_steps-legacy-only phrasing.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: The round-1 fix (_seed_legacy_phase_task_history seeding only the historical completed_steps phases) fully resolves the legacy-cutover history-loss bug and the one-time cutover remains self-healing / eventually converges for a pre-s5 legacy run. — Traced two consecutive Stop-hook invocations for a legacy config with current_step='build', completed_steps=['project','design','plan'], no phase_tasks[], where build genuinely is NOT yet complete at the first Stop event. Invocation 1: cutover fires, historical_phases=['design','plan','project'] get seeded as 'done', but no entry is created for 'build' (excluded by construction). _detect_phase_complete('build', ...) is False, so _run_phase_completion is not called this round -- no phase_tasks[] entry for build is created. Invocation 2: phase_tasks[] now has 3 valid entries, so phase_tasks_has_usable_entries() flips True, and the cutover guard (current_phase is None and not usable) never fires again. phase_tasks_progress() only derives 'current' from phases already present in phase_tasks[], so current_phase is permanently None from this point -- build is never picked up again.
findings.suggestion: Also seed a non-terminal (in_progress) phase_tasks[] entry for current_phase itself in the same write as the historical entries, so a later invocation's phase_tasks_progress() can resolve it as current without the cutover firing again; the existing update-step call for a same-round completion then finds and upgrades that same entry to done via the standard phase+splitId=None match.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: The new direct write in _seed_legacy_phase_task_history is a safe way to persist the legacy-history seed against shipwright_run_config.json. — config_io.py documents the established contract for shipwright_run_config.json: writes go through save_run_config, which is atomic (tmp + os.replace) and whose advisory run-config lock is held by callers (update_step, phase_task_lifecycle). _seed_legacy_phase_task_history did neither -- a plain run_config_path.write_text(...) with no lock and no tmp+replace, against the same file every other writer in the tree treats as lock-protected and atomically replaced. A process kill mid-write (Stop hooks can be time-boxed/killed) can leave a truncated/corrupt config, and a genuine race with a concurrent update-step subprocess is a lost-update window.
findings.suggestion: Route the write through the same shared advisory lock (lib.file_lock on the shipwright_run_config.json.lock path every other writer coordinates through) and the same atomic-write primitive (lib.atomic_write.durable_atomic_write) instead of a bare write_text -- both live in shared/scripts/lib, so no ADR-045 cross-plugin boundary issue, unlike the phase_tasks[]-shape duplication elsewhere in this diff.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: state.py's detect_current_phase and suggest_iterate.py, which read-only-recompute their own legacy cutover on every call, could share the same self-disabling-write failure class as generate_handoff_on_stop.py's cutover. — Traced both readers: neither persists anything -- they recompute fresh on every call, so they cannot self-disable the way the Stop-hook's new write-path can.

Claim under doubt: config_factory.create_config's standalone-to-driven merge cutover shares the same current-phase-orphaning failure mode the Stop-hook cutover had. — create_config's merge always produces a fresh schemaVersion:2 config with a full phase_tasks[] set, including an entry for the actually-current phase via the ordinary v2 lifecycle machinery -- so phase_tasks_progress()'s schemaVersion-gated branch correctly resolves 'current' going forward. It does not share the Stop-hook cutover's failure mode.

Claim under doubt: The phase_quality._engagement.py executionCount=1 stamp reinstatement and the completed_phases_with_fallback -> completed_phases rename could have left an orphaned old-name reference or an inconsistent call site somewhere in the diff. — Checked all call sites (design_checks.py, compliance_compliance.py, convert_configs_to_events.py) -- all route through the renamed shared function, grep-clean for the old name.

create_config` marks a standalone-completed project as `status: "skipped"` (via `_build_initial_phase_task`, which per `_engagement.py` has `executionCount: 0` and no execution history), while every other standalone-completed phase gets a `build_v1_phase_task(..., "done")` entry with `executionCount: 1` — which `_task_has_run` treats as "ran". Since s5 removed the `completed_steps` union that used to keep the skipped-project engaged, `phase_is_engaged("project", ...)` is now False for exactly the project phase on the same run where design/plan/build (all equally completed standalone) are engaged. Phase-Quality silently audits fewer phases for `project` than for its siblings on the identical config shape.
findings.suggestion: Either bump the skipped initial task's `executionCount` to 1 (it did run — standalone), or mark merged tasks `skipped` + an explicit marker, so all standalone-completed phases engage uniformly. Add a test asserting `phase_is_engaged` for every phase in `prior_completed` post-merge.  2. `state.detect_current_phase` and `suggest_iterate` lack the one-time legacy cutover every other reader got

findings.finding: generate_handoff_on_stop` and `config_factory.create_config` both gained a deliberate one-time `current_step`/`completed_steps` cutover for pre-s5 configs already on disk (so a legacy standalone run self-heals by triggering `update-step`, which seeds `phase_tasks[]`). `detect_current_phase` and `suggest_iterate` got no equivalent: a pre-s5 standalone config mid-pipeline now misreports its phase (the changed test itself pins `detect_current_phase == "build"` for a run whose `current_step` was `changelog`, and `test_detect_phase_v1_only_completed_steps...` pins a finished run reporting `"build"` instead of `"complete"`). A finished standalone run reading `"build"` forever is a user-visible wrong answer, and unlike the handoff path there is no mechanism that ever corrects it — the config never gets a `phase_tasks[]` write if nothing else touches it.
findings.suggestion: Either give both readers the same gated cutover (`current_step is None and not phase_tasks_has_usable_entries(...)`), or document explicitly in the s5 ADR why these two readers are permitted to permanently misreport legacy on-disk configs, and confirm no consumer of `detect_current_phase`'s "complete" answer gates anything.  3. `_upsert_v1_phase_task` treats `skipped` as non-terminal when clearing `completedAt

findings.finding: if status in {"done", "failed"}: completedAt = now else: completedAt = None` — a status of `"skipped"` (terminal in `FINISHED_STATUSES` everywhere else) would land in the else-branch and clear `completedAt`, producing a "skipped-but-never-finished" entry. Currently unreachable because `update_step` only ever passes `in_progress`/`done`/`failed`, but the helper is exported and unit-tested as a general API, and the terminal-set duplication will silently diverge if a caller ever passes `skipped`.
findings.suggestion: Reuse the shared `FINISHED_STATUSES` constant (or add `"skipped"` to the terminal set) for the `completedAt` decision.  4. Post-test fallback in `suggest_iterate` is silently dead for legacy configs

findings.finding: With the v1 fallback removed, `completed_steps` is whatever `_phase_tasks_progress` returned — empty for a config with no usable `phase_tasks[]`. The "post-test fallback" (delegate to `classify_for_iterate` once test is done) therefore never fires for a pre-s5 standalone config, reintroducing exactly the "stale limbo" of silently-dropped post-test prompts that the fallback was added to fix — but only for that legacy population. Same root cause as finding 2, lower blast radius (advisory hint only).  5. `test_shipwright_run_e2e.py` final-state assertion accepts `skipped` without asserting which

completed = {t["phase"] for t in config["phase_tasks"] if ... status in ("done", "skipped")}` — an implementation that marked a phase `skipped` when it should have been `done` (e.g., a wrongly-firing skip path) still passes. Pre-s5 the test asserted exact set equality against `completed_steps` contents; it now can't distinguish done from skipped at all.
findings.suggestion: Also assert every completed phase's status is `done` (or pin the expected per-phase statuses) for this greenfield e2e.

findings.finding: The standalone-to-driven merge still reads `completed_steps` when `phase_tasks[]` is absent/unusable. This directly violates the acceptance criterion that no reader anywhere keys on the retired fields, and retains the mode/shape-conditional authority the specification explicitly rejects.
findings.suggestion: Perform legacy conversion in an explicit migration/backfill before this path, then make `create_config()` consume only `phase_tasks[]` and remove this fallback.

findings.finding: The Stop hook still reads `current_step` and `completed_steps` for “one-time cutover.” Thus a legacy config’s phase completion is still driven by the old fields, rather than `phase_tasks[]`, contrary to both “retarget first” and “No reader anywhere” requirements.
findings.suggestion: Backfill legacy configs before hook execution (or make a dedicated migration command mandatory) and remove this fallback branch so the hook only derives progress from `phase_tasks[]`.  The schema documentation and new-path tests are otherwise substantially aligned with the intended retargeting, but these intentional legacy read paths fail a core acceptance criterion. Ship with fixes after removing or externalizing the legacy-field reads.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

external_code.disposition: Ran 3 rounds (GLM+OpenAI each); round-3's findings recorded here are the last actual external pass. All 5 round-3 findings fixed or dispositioned in the ADR's External-Code-Review-Findings table (2 rejected-with-reason repeats of the same AC-literalism objection, argued at length; 5 fixed with regression tests). A 4th round was deliberately not re-run -- see ADR for why.
